sourceValue: 28 days (5.6 weeks) for a 5-day week
comparisonNote: Employers can count bank holidays as part of these 28 days.
sourceQuote: Most workers who work a 5-day week must receive at least 28 days' paid annual leave a year.

sourceValue: 4 working weeks
comparisonNote: Public holidays are a separate entitlement on top of this.
sourceQuote: Most employees are entitled to 4 working weeks' of annual leave each year.

sourceValue: 24 working days, counted on a 6-day week
comparisonNote: The law counts Monday to Saturday as working days ("Werktage"). Public holidays are on top of this.
sourceQuote: Der Urlaub beträgt jährlich mindestens 24 Werktage.

sourceValue: 4 times the hours worked per week
comparisonNote: Stated in hours. For a 40-hour week this is 160 hours.
sourceQuote: a minimum of 4 times the number of hours they work per week

sourceValue: No right to paid leave on bank holidays
comparisonNote: There are 8 bank holidays in England and Wales in 2026 (10 in Scotland and in Northern Ireland), but there is no legal right to have them off. Employers can count them within the 28 days of annual leave.
sourceQuote: Bank or public holidays do not have to be given as paid leave.

sourceValue: 10 public holidays
detail: For each one, the employer chooses: a paid day off on the day, a paid day off within a month, an extra day of annual leave, or an extra day's pay.
comparisonNote: Part-time workers qualify after working 40 hours in the previous 5 weeks.
sourceQuote: There are 10 public holidays in Ireland each year (increased from 9 in 2022).

sourceValue: 9 nationwide public holidays
detail: Pay continues for working time lost to a public holiday (EFZG § 2).
comparisonNote: Each federal state sets its own holidays, so some states have more than 9.
sourceTitle: National holidays (Federal Ministry of the Interior)
sourceQuote: Under the federal states' legislation on Sundays and holidays, nine public holidays are observed nationwide

sourceValue: No legal right to a day off on public holidays
comparisonNote: Whether public holidays are days off is set by the collective labour agreement (CAO) or the employment contract.
sourceQuote: Public holidays are not specified in law as mandatory days off.

sourceValue: 52 weeks
detail: Statutory Maternity Pay for up to 39 weeks: 90% of average weekly earnings for 6 weeks, then £194.32 a week or 90% of average weekly earnings (whichever is lower) for 33 weeks. The last 13 weeks are unpaid.
sourceQuote: Statutory Maternity Leave is 52 weeks.

sourceValue: 26 weeks, plus up to 16 weeks' additional leave
detail: Maternity Benefit from the Department of Social Protection covers the first 26 weeks, if you have enough PRSI contributions. The additional 16 weeks are unpaid. Any pay from the employer depends on the contract.
sourceQuote: As an employee, you have the right to take 26 weeks' maternity leave if you become pregnant. You also have the right to take up to 16 weeks' additional maternity leave.

sourceValue: 6 weeks before birth and 8 weeks after (12 after in some cases)
detail: Maternity pay (Mutterschaftsgeld) plus an employer top-up together match average net pay (MuSchG § 20).
comparisonNote: Either parent can also take unpaid parental leave (Elternzeit) until the child turns 3, with a separate state parental allowance.
sourceQuote: Der Arbeitgeber darf eine Frau bis zum Ablauf von acht Wochen nach der Entbindung nicht beschäftigen.

sourceValue: At least 16 weeks: 6 before the due date and at least 10 after birth
detail: The employer keeps paying salary and receives a benefit from the UWV.
sourceQuote: Your pregnant employee is entitled to pregnancy leave and maternity leave (in total at least 16 weeks)

sourceValue: Up to 2 weeks
detail: Statutory Paternity Pay is £194.32 a week or 90% of average weekly earnings, whichever is lower.
sourceQuote: You can take up to 2 weeks' leave.

sourceValue: 2 weeks
detail: The employer does not have to pay. Paternity Benefit from the Department of Social Protection is available with enough PRSI contributions.
sourceQuote: Paternity leave gives new parents 2 weeks off work.

sourceValue: No separate statutory paternity leave
comparisonNote: Fathers can take parental leave (Elternzeit), open to either parent until the child turns 3, with a state parental allowance (Elterngeld). A proposed paid leave for partners after birth ("Familienstartzeit") has not become law.
sourceTitle: Parental Allowance and Parental Leave Act, section 15 (BEEG § 15)
sourceQuote: Der Anspruch auf Elternzeit besteht bis zur Vollendung des dritten Lebensjahres eines Kindes.

sourceValue: 1 week of partner leave, plus 5 weeks of additional partner leave
detail: The first week is paid in full by the employer. The additional 5 weeks are paid at 70% of salary through a UWV benefit, taken within 6 months of the birth.
sourceQuote: During this period of leave you must continue to pay 100% of the employee's salary.

sourceValue: Up to 28 weeks
detail: Statutory Sick Pay is £123.25 a week or 80% of normal weekly earnings, whichever is lower.
sourceQuote: It's paid for up to 28 weeks.

sourceValue: 5 days a year
detail: 70% of normal pay, up to €110 a day, after 13 weeks with the employer. Longer illness may be covered by the state's Illness Benefit.
sourceTitle: Sick leave and sick pay (Citizens Information)
sourceQuote: Sick pay is paid by your employer at 70% of your normal pay up to a maximum of €110 a day.

sourceValue: Up to 6 weeks
detail: Full pay for the hours the employee would have worked, after 4 weeks of employment. After that, health insurance sickness benefit takes over.
sourceQuote: Anspruch auf Entgeltfortzahlung im Krankheitsfall bis zur Dauer von sechs Wochen

sourceValue: Up to 2 years
detail: At least 70% of wages, topped up to the minimum wage in the first year.
sourceQuote: you are required to pay at least 70% of their wages for up to 2 years

sourceValue: 3% employer minimum under automatic enrolment
detail: Of earnings between £6,240 and £50,270 a year, for most schemes. The total minimum, with the employee's share, is 8%.
sourceQuote: The minimum your employer pays: 3%

sourceValue: 1.5% of salary under auto-enrolment (MyFutureFund), rising to 6% by year 10
detail: Since 1 January 2026, for employees aged 23 to 60 earning €20,000 or more who do not already pay into a pension through payroll. Employer contributions stop at a salary of €80,000.
sourceQuote: In the first year, you and your employer will pay 1.5% of your annual salary. This will increase to 6% by year 10.

sourceValue: No required employer contribution to a workplace pension
comparisonNote: Employees can ask to put part of their pay into a workplace pension, and the employer must then add 15% of the amount where it saves social security contributions. Separately, employers pay into the state pension insurance, which is not a workplace pension.
sourceQuote: Der Arbeitgeber muss 15 Prozent des umgewandelten Entgelts zusätzlich als Arbeitgeberzuschuss … weiterleiten, soweit er durch die Entgeltumwandlung Sozialversicherungsbeiträge einspart.

sourceValue: No general legal duty to offer a pension
comparisonNote: Many Dutch employees are in a compulsory industry pension fund, and a collective labour agreement (CAO) can also require a pension. Where neither applies, the employer can choose.
sourceQuote: In certain business sectors, companies have to offer their employees a pension.

sourceValue: 1 week for each year of service between 2 and 12 years
comparisonNote: Rises by a week for each year of service, up to 12 weeks.
sourceQuote: one week's notice for each year if employed between 2 and 12 years

sourceValue: 2 weeks for 2 to 5 years of service
sourceQuote: 2 years to 5 years: 2 weeks

sourceValue: 1 month, to the end of a calendar month
comparisonNote: Ending at the end of a month can make the notice longer in practice.
sourceQuote: zwei Jahre bestanden hat, einen Monat zum Ende eines Kalendermonats

sourceValue: 1 month for less than 5 years of service
comparisonNote: Rises by a month for every 5 years of service, up to 4 months.
sourceTitle: Notice period in case of dismissal (Business.gov.nl)
sourceQuote: The minimum notice period is at least 1 month.
